topics.title: Electric ferries gain momentum in the US
topics.summary: New electric ferries are arriving in the United States, including designs that can lift above the water. Supporters say replacing diesel vessels could cut emissions and improve local air quality.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you rather take a quiet electric ferry, a classic boat with lots of character, or one that actually lifts above the waves? What would make a short crossing feel like part of the adventure?

topics.title: Queen of Spain butterflies arrive in Britain
topics.summary: Thousands of golden Queen of Spain butterflies have arrived in Britain this year. Experts are watching to see whether this striking visitor can establish a lasting population.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an unexpected new butterfly or bird began showing up where you live, would you be excited, curious, or a little cautious? Which wild visitor would make you stop and look twice?

topics.title: A Cumbrian hill farm makes its organic shift
topics.summary: A hill farm near Tebay in Cumbria is formally converting to organic certification after long using organic principles. The change highlights the practical challenges and values behind lower-input farming.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you ran a small farm or garden, what would matter most: growing unusual food, protecting wildlife, making a living, trying new methods, or keeping old traditions alive?

topics.title: Workplaces weigh AI agent co-workers
topics.summary: Companies are testing AI agents for tasks from executive assistance to chief-of-staff work. The experiments promise efficiency while raising questions about how human teams will adapt.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI helper joined your team, what harmless chore would you gladly hand over first: scheduling, sorting messages, making lists, research, or reminding everyone where they left things?

topics.title: Psychics debate AI-generated readings
topics.summary: Some psychics say AI-generated readings cannot replace the empathy and personal connection they see as central to their work. The debate is another example of AI entering highly human-facing services.
topics.discussionPrompt: For advice that feels personal, do you care more about the answer itself or who delivers it? Could a clever app ever feel as comforting as a real conversation?

topics.title: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart
topics.summary: DoorDash has agreed to buy Instacart for $17 billion, a deal that would combine two major delivery businesses. The companies say grocery delivery remains difficult to make work smoothly online.
topics.discussionPrompt: What would make grocery delivery genuinely useful to you: better substitutions, lower fees, faster delivery, reusable packaging, recipes that use what you already have, or something else?

topics.title: US growth beats forecasts as inflation rises
topics.summary: New Commerce Department data showed US economic growth outpacing expectations in the third quarter, while inflation reached 3.7%. The mixed picture arrives alongside weaker consumer sentiment.
topics.discussionPrompt: When people say the economy is doing well, what do you notice first in everyday life: grocery prices, wages, job options, rent, small businesses, or something totally different?

topics.title: England beat Sri Lanka in tri-series finale
topics.summary: Ben Duckett scored 167 and Liam Dawson took four wickets as England beat Sri Lanka by 55 runs. The win was England's consolation result in the one-day tri-series.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a sports comeback satisfying to watch: one player having an incredible day, the whole team finding its rhythm, a clever tactic, or a tense finish?

topics.title: Pasifika fans bring colour to Rugby League World Cup
topics.summary: Supporters from Pacific communities in western Sydney are bringing colour, music, and strong local connection to the Rugby League World Cup as their home nations compete.
topics.discussionPrompt: What turns a sporting event into a community celebration: flags, music, family traditions, food, friendly rivalries, travelling together, or the chance to cheer for a place that feels like home?

topics.title: Tiny Melbourne apartment wins design recognition
topics.summary: A compact Melbourne basement was transformed into an award-winning apartment with less than 40 square metres of floor space. The design uses careful planning and spatial tricks to make a small home feel lively.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you had to make a very small apartment feel bigger, what would you prioritize: hidden storage, big windows, flexible furniture, a great kitchen, a cozy reading nook, or bold colours?
